1.title: A Man Asleep - Reimagined Poster
1.description: I wanted to revisit the poster for the film 'Un Homme qui dort' (1974), a classic that struck me with its unique atmosphere. I kept the original typography that I love, but completely reimagined the visual in Photoshop: textured, grainy close-ups that, to me, better convey boredom and introspection than the usual emptiness. A way of telling isolation through texture.

Mockup presentation of the reimagined 'A Man Asleep' poster.

3.title: Poster Tribute: Sade - Diamond Life
3.description: Diamond Life by Sade (1984) is an album I truly appreciate. I wanted to pay tribute through a poster created in Photoshop that captures that distinctive soul/jazz elegance, with retro treatment and sepia tones evoking vinyl and nostalgia.
gallery: Original tribute poster for Sade's Diamond Life album.

4.title: UX Design: Veco App
4.context: SAE Project BUT2 - Mobile app design
4.description: Team project  My role: visual design in Figma for Veco, a peer-to-peer electric vehicle rental app. Translated soft mobility and ecology values into an intuitive interface. Green and natural color palette to anchor the eco-friendly universe. Mockups cover the complete journey (geolocation, booking, user profile) with design focused on reassurance and ease of use.
gallery: Veco app presentation: Overview of the visual identity and design system for the electric mobility app.
Welcome and registration screen: Clean login and registration interface showcasing the app's visual identity from launch.
Vehicle geolocation: Main map view displaying all available vehicles in real-time around the user's position.
Vehicle selection and quote: Detailed vehicle card showing characteristics (model, range) and clear trip price estimate.
Guidance to pickup point: Integrated GPS navigation guiding the user (pedestrian route) to the exact vehicle location.
Filtering by 'Bike-Taxi' category: Activating the specific 'Bike-Taxi' mode via selector, filtering the map to show only nearby bike-taxis.
Destination input: Intuitive search interface for choosing arrival point or selecting a favorite destination.
Confirmation and Payment: Trip summary screen with secure payment method selection before final confirmation.
Help center and support: Quick access to customer service and FAQ via help button for user assistance.
Profile and Settings: Configuration menu for managing user account, notification preferences and trip history.

5.title: UI Design & Branding: Real Estate Agency
5.description: Team project  My role: visual identity and mockup design in Figma. This project had an interesting constraint: thinking about SEO from the design phase. Not just making it pretty, but creating a structure that search engines would also appreciate. I designed the complete visual identity  logo, Design System  ensuring everything remained lightweight and performant. The mockups leverage visual hierarchy to naturally guide users while facilitating indexing.

7.title: Open Heart, NGO Visual Identity
7.context: SAE Project BUT2 - Visual identity creation
7.description: Open Heart is a fictional NGO fighting against domestic violence. I created the complete visual identity in Illustrator: logo, brand guidelines, and also wrote a portrait article in InDesign giving voice to a survivor. The name evokes a judgment-free space for speaking out. My challenge: finding the right balance between a reassuring and professional image that inspires trust and kindness.

parts.title: The Challenge
parts.subtitle: Giving a voice to all victims
paragraphs: Behind every statistic, there is a person. A person seeking to be heard. That is the premise behind Open Heart: a fictional NGO dedicated to domestic violence victims, available 24/7. In a landscape dominated by established organisations like Fondation des Femmes or Elles Imaginent, the challenge was to build a strong visual identity and a 360° communication strategy capable of standing out.

parts.title: Strategy & 360° Communication
paragraphs: Building an NGO from scratch means first understanding the environment it will operate in. Before any visual creation, I took part in developing a comprehensive strategy.

It began with a thorough competitive audit: a comparative analysis of three major NGOs  Fondation des Femmes, Elles Imaginent and Women's Aid  covering their brand guidelines, editorial lines, social media and communication strategies. A deep dive to identify the sector's codes, but also its blind spots.

From there, we defined Open Heart's positioning: an organisation that welcomes all victims with a warm, empathetic, non-judgmental tone. This editorial stance was translated into a complete framework  tone, themes, content formats, multichannel strategy  tailored to each platform: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X.

Finally, a 360° campaign was designed to bring this identity to life: awareness posters, two 30-second video spots, newsletters and social media content, all structured around a consistent publication schedule.

parts.title: UX/UI Design & Visual Identity
paragraphs: A visual identity is not just about aesthetics. For an NGO like Open Heart, every design choice is a choice of welcome.

The responsive website was designed so that everyone finds their place immediately: a clear information architecture, navigation structured by user profile  victims, witnesses, professionals, donors. Desktop and mobile mockups were created in Figma, guided by a single question: can someone in distress find what they need, quickly, without effort?

The design system follows the same logic. Purple  historically associated with the fight against violence  pairs with white and soft tones to create a reassuring visual space. The logo  a stylised heart  evokes both listening and openness, without ever slipping into pathos.

Among the features designed for the most vulnerable users: an emergency button enabling instant redirection to an innocuous page  an ordinary Google search  to protect victims who might visit the site in a dangerous situation. A technical detail, but a deeply human decision.
Finally, educational content was structured to ease access to information: articles, anonymous testimonials, legal and psychological resources  designed to be found, understood, and used.

parts.title: Impact & Learnings
paragraphs: This was one of the most demanding projects of my studies  not technically, but humanly. Working on a cause as sensitive as domestic violence means never losing sight of what is at stake behind every creative choice.

I came away with a broader understanding of what it means to communicate for a committed organisation: adapting tone to each channel  institutional on LinkedIn, warm and empathetic on Instagram , designing user journeys built for a vulnerable audience, and holding together strategic rigour, documentary research and human sensitivity.

The outcome: a strong and consistent visual identity, a strategy deployed across all channels, a website built for accessibility and safety, and a full campaign including video spots, posters, social media content and newsletters.

8.title: Gummo  Film Poster
8.description: Gummo (1997) by Harmony Korine is a film that doesn't leave you indifferent. Experimental, disturbing, yet strangely poetic. I wanted to create a poster in Photoshop and Illustrator that captures this unique atmosphere: the trashy and nostalgic imagery, the desaturated 90s colors, that disenchanted vibe.

10.title: FLEMME  Short Film
10.context: Nikon Film Festival 2025 Contest  Theme: Superpower
10.description: Fantasy and engaged comedy short film created for the Nikon Film Festival 2025 on the theme 'Superpower'. Luc, a lazy twenty-something, lives a life of total inertia between unemployment, TV and video games. Selfish, lazy and antisocial, he possesses an extraordinary gift: he's nearly omnipotent and can modify the reality of anything he touches.

14.title: Alicia Keys 20th Anniversary Box Set
14.context: SAE401 project, IUT de Bobigny, MMI department
14.description: As a team of three, we designed the complete visual identity of an anniversary box set celebrating Alicia Keys' 20 years on stage: typographic research, an illustrated character, CD sleeves, stickers, a concert poster and a collector's vinyl. Every piece follows a single art direction, from packaging to large-format street display.

subProjects.title: Defining the world
subProjects.description: It all starts with words. Renaissance, Fire, Prestige, Heritage: four themes that steer the whole project. The board explores three typographic directions (bold, calligraphic, minimal) before settling on a contemporary luxury sans-serif, strong enough to carry twenty years of career without overpowering it.

subProjects.title: Giving the project a face
subProjects.description: Once the direction was set, the artist had to be embodied without falling into portraiture. The board traces how the character was built: flat design references, a geometric face, refined proportions, down to a restricted palette (ochre, black, brown, terracotta) that became the colour signature of the whole box set.

subProjects.title: Designing the stage
subProjects.description: The box set is more than an object: it accompanies a tour. The proposed stage design puts Alicia Keys at the piano in the middle of a sober stage, with a glossy gold floor and gold LED lighting. The space becomes a natural extension of the visual identity: luxury, warmth, presence.

subProjects.title: Cover research
subProjects.description: Several attempts at the box set's gold cover: different framings, photo treatments and ways of integrating the illustrated character. These explorations tested how well the gold palette held together before the final direction was chosen.

subProjects.title: Collector's stickers
subProjects.description: The illustrated character finds its first real use on round collector's stickers. The arched '20TH ANNIVERSARY TOUR' lettering roots each piece in the codes of premium merchandise: objects made to be kept.

subProjects.title: The official artwork
subProjects.description: All the research comes together in this artwork: the typographic identity, the palette, the character, the golden mood. The vertical layout is designed to work on the physical box set as well as on communication media. It is the centrepiece of the project.

subProjects.title: Concert poster
subProjects.description: A simple, direct poster announcing the anniversary tour, applying the box set's visual identity to a classic poster format.

subProjects.title: Large-format street display
subProjects.description: A final robustness test: the poster shown on a bus shelter in a real setting. At this scale, every choice of composition and contrast shows. The artwork holds: the type stays legible, the image keeps its density, and the golden identity stands out in the street.

subProjects.title: The centrepiece
subProjects.description: The collector's vinyl closes the box set, and the project. A prestige object by nature, it carries the visual identity in its most finished form. The round record echoes the stickers, and the gold palette recalls every piece produced: twenty years of music brought together in a single object.

17.title: Iris: a liquid glass sculpture
17.context: Personal project, generative art and video
17.description: Iris is a liquid glass sculpture that only exists in a shader: bubbles that merge and split apart, computed in real time in TouchDesigner and driven by music. The project comes in two parts: a studio version, then Anomalie, where Iris appears in a real landscape, filmed as if by a 2003 camcorder.
gallery: Iris as the bass drops back in: the bubbles swell and merge as the reflections flare.
Iris during the quiet passage: two floating bubbles joined by a thread of matter.
Iris mid-pulse, its iridescent surface bent by the rhythm.

parts.title: The idea
parts.subtitle: A material rather than an object
paragraphs: I wanted an image you would want to watch on repeat, somewhere between a drop of mercury, a soap bubble and a lava lamp. Not a recognisable object, but a living, glossy material that keeps changing shape without ever quite repeating itself.
The palette follows from that: iridescent peach, pink, lilac and cyan reflections over a magenta gradient that slides into midnight blue. A saturated palette, yet soft enough to stay elegant.

parts.title: Sculpting with maths
parts.subtitle: No 3D model, just a shader
paragraphs: Iris was never modelled. The whole image is computed by a GLSL shader in TouchDesigner, using a technique called raymarching: for every pixel, a ray leaves the camera and steps forward until it touches a surface described by a formula.

That formula joins seven spheres with a smooth union: when two spheres get close, they melt into each other instead of intersecting, which is what makes it look liquid. The reflections imitate the thin film of a soap bubble, whose colour shifts with the viewing angle.

parts.title: Making the material dance
parts.subtitle: The music drives the shape
paragraphs: Iris is tied to the music. The track is analysed ahead of time, frame by frame: the bass swells the bubbles until they merge, the highs make their surface shiver, and every hit pushes them apart for an instant as the reflections flash.
The fifteen-second excerpt is built on contrast: eight quiet seconds where the bubbles float in suspension, then the bass crashes back in and the sculpture flares up.

parts.title: The loop
parts.subtitle: Eight seconds, no cut
paragraphs: The studio version is vertical, 4:5. Without the music it is a perfect eight-second loop: the last frame joins the first exactly, so the video plays forever with no visible cut.
Every frame is rendered without dropping any, at 60 frames per second, exported as ProRes and then converted to H.264.

parts.title: Anomalie
parts.subtitle: A fake tape from 2003
paragraphs: Once the sculpture worked, I wanted to put it up against the real world. The starting point is a river shot filmed on a phone. I cut out the sky, erased the clouds and tinted the rest pink in a shader, to give Iris room to float. Then I blended it into the landscape, with a reflection in the river, shadows and grain, so it belongs to the image instead of sitting on top of it.

Everything else is about ageing the image: a 4:3 crop, the shake of a handheld camera, lens distortion, then the camcorder display on top, with "REC", the battery, the counter and the date, "14. 8.2003". The final render imitates a MiniDV tape, at 768 × 576 and 25 frames per second, with its colours and video noise. It looks like a holiday video that caught something unexplained.

video.caption: Anomalie · 10 s · with sound
video.label: Anomalie: Iris in the sky, filmed as if by a MiniDV camcorder

parts.title: Behind the scenes
parts.subtitle: Nine steps, from phone to camcorder
paragraphs: Anomalie is built layer by layer in TouchDesigner: the original footage, the sky cut-out, the cleaned sky, the sculpture, compositing and grading, the 4:3 crop, the handheld camera, the camcorder display and finally the MiniDV render. In this video the grid fills up step by step, the camera follows each new layer, then pulls back to show them all together.

video.caption: Behind the scenes of Anomalie · 16 s
video.label: The nine steps used to build Anomalie in TouchDesigner

18.title: Uzbek Portrait: a mosaic of crafts
18.description: A painted portrait of an Uzbek man, recomposed live by a grid of tiles. Each tile borrows a Central Asian craft: ikat, suzani, girih, Samarkand ceramics and letters of the Arabic-Persian alphabet. Every three seconds the mosaic reshuffles in a wave that starts from the face. Computed in a GLSL shader in TouchDesigner.
galleryDescriptions: Balanced: half of the cells keep the painting, the other half turn into pattern.
Dense: almost the whole figure is covered in tiles.
Fine mosaic: ten columns instead of six, smaller tiles.
Cut out: the figure alone, without the painting's background.

parts.title: The idea
parts.subtitle: A painting that rearranges itself
paragraphs: The starting point is Enigmatriz's work: a grid of tiles laid over an image, where some cells keep the painting and others turn into pattern. I wanted to take that principle and give it an identity, that of Central Asia, starting from a painted portrait of an Uzbek man in a striped chapan.

Before the tiles, the image is graded automatically: the program measures its blacks and whites, removes part of the colour cast and adds a little contrast, so the painting's colours hold up against the patterns.

parts.title: The tiles
parts.subtitle: Five Central Asian crafts
paragraphs: Each tile borrows a craft from the region: ikat and its woven, blurred-edge patterns, the embroidered medallions of suzani, the geometric interlace of girih, the glazes of Samarkand ceramics, and letters of the Arabic-Persian alphabet once used to write Chagatai, the old Uzbek language.

The colours come from traditional dyes and pigments: madder, pomegranate, saffron, indigo, lapis lazuli and turquoise. For the letter tiles, each character is ranked by how much ink it holds: the painting's dark areas get the densest letters, the light areas the lightest.

parts.title: The cut-out
parts.subtitle: The figure, set on a new background
paragraphs: The tiles only cover the figure. To cut him out, the program starts from the top of the image and follows the dark brown area connected to it. The beard and the black stripes of the chapan are spared, because they don't touch the background or don't share its warm hue.

Once cut out, the figure can be set on several backgrounds computed in the shader: the original background cleaned of its grain, a ganch wall, the carved stucco of Bukhara's palaces, black velvet adorned with girih and gold lines, the background repainted in oil, or a black paint, the one used for these versions. There is also a transparent version, ready for editing.

parts.title: The animation
parts.subtitle: A wave that starts from the face
paragraphs: Every three seconds the mosaic reshuffles: some cells turn back into painting, others change pattern. The change doesn't happen all at once, it starts from the face and spreads to the edges, with a small random delay for each tile.
Each video lasts twelve seconds, four cycles. It is rendered frame by frame at 30 frames per second, so no frame is dropped whatever the computer's speed, then assembled at 1080 px wide.

parts.title: The variations
parts.subtitle: Eight compositions
paragraphs: Three settings are enough to change the image completely: the number of columns, the share of cells left intact and the random seed. I drew eight compositions from them, from the sparest, where three cells out of four keep the painting, to the densest, where almost everything becomes pattern.
